description:
memory.rs:121-130 declares Inner.objects/states/change_log as HashMap<(&'static str, String), ...>. Every accessor (current_state line 134, bump_state 140, objects_mut 149, objects_ref 160, change_log_mut 168) takes the account_id as &str and then calls .to_owned() to build the tuple key for HashMap::get/entry. This allocates a new String on every read of an existing entry — including every get_state / get_changes / get_objects call.

Idiomatic Rust avoids this in one of three ways:
  1. Nested map: HashMap<&'static str, HashMap<Id, HashMap<Id, Value>>> — outer key borrows as &str, no allocation.
  2. Use Id (which is the right key type) instead of String — Id is a newtype over a small string; .get with &(type_name, id) avoids the .to_owned() if you implement Borrow.
  3. HashMap::raw_entry_mut (nightly) or a (&str, &str) key with hashbrown's Borrow-tuple equivalent.

Engineering cost: every read-path JMAP method does at least one allocation per typed accessor, plus another inside bump_state on every mutation, none of which is observable in tests but shows up under load. The pattern propagates: same shape in canonical jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs:111-115, so the fix needs to land on the canonical first per workspace propagation rule.

Why this matters when it stays as-is: silent allocation in every hot-path lookup is the textbook example of a non-idiomatic map shape. A reader writing a real production backend cannot copy this pattern without inheriting the same waste.
title: Inner's (&'static str, String) map keys force allocation on every read
